category_title: Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder experiencing psychomotor retardation, cognitive disorganization, and emotional volatility
minimal_context: The student and tutor are sitting together to organize the student's binder and backpack before starting their schoolwork.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's start by organizing your binder and backpack so we can begin your schoolwork.

STUDENT: (Shuffles papers from side to side) My backpack is a mess. It's just bits of paper in whirlwind in here.

TUTOR: Just look through it and decide what you need to keep and what you can throw away.

STUDENT: I don't know what to throw away. I can't make decisions about my work right now, I can't organize this material.

TUTOR: Okay, let's just find some binder paper so we can start writing the first assignment.

STUDENT: (Ignores the inch of paper in the open binder right in front of him and stands up) I'm going to my room to get some. The family cat is being fairly annoying anyway.

options.A: Issue the sanction of a verbal warning regarding the student's behavior of leaving the workspace during the session.
options.B: Tell the student which subject and assignments to work on, then ask them to review the tasks and choose one they want help with first.
options.C: Provide explicit teaching of organizational strategies for the binder and backpack using evidence-informed interventions before starting.
options.D: Joke extensively about the disorganized backpack and laugh at oneself before starting the schoolwork.
